records.name: Assumption-Driven Delivery
records.definition: Shipping on untested assumptions about behavior instead of validating that requirements are met.

records.name: Environment-Sensitive Behavior
records.definition: Behavior that changes with the host environment, so the same run yields different results elsewhere.

records.name: Example-Only Testing
records.definition: Testing only a few hand-picked examples instead of properties that must hold across all inputs.

records.name: Floating Dependencies

distinctFrom.reason: Floating dependencies make builds unreproducible through unpinned versions, while flaky test normalization accepts intermittent failures by rerunning them.

records.definition: Depending on unpinned, floating dependency versions, so builds are not reproducible.

records.name: Hidden Behavior
records.definition: Behavior triggered by hidden state or side effects, so outcomes surprise callers.

records.name: Hidden IO
records.definition: Performing input/output inside a supposedly pure function, hiding side effects from callers.

records.name: Hidden Time/Randomness/Global State
records.definition: Reading the clock, randomness, or global state inside a computation, making its output nondeterministic.

records.name: Implementation-Only Testing

distinctFrom.reason: Implementation-only testing checks today's behavior instead of the contract, while a mock mirage checks calls on mocks instead of behavior.

records.definition: Testing only against the current implementation's behavior rather than the specified contract.

records.name: Informal Validation Only
records.definition: Relying only on informal checks and testing where a formal proof of correctness is warranted.

records.name: Side Effects
records.definition: Producing observable side effects in an expression, so it cannot be replaced by its value.

records.name: Unchecked Dynamic Code
records.definition: Running dynamically generated or evaluated code that static analysis cannot inspect for defects.

records.name: Undefined Behavior
records.definition: Relying on operations whose result is unspecified, so outcomes vary unpredictably across runs or platforms.

records.name: Untested Implementation
records.definition: Shipping code with no tests, so its conformance to the specification is unverified.

records.name: Behavior Validation
records.definition: The ability to confirm a system behaves as its specification requires.

records.name: Broad Input Exploration
records.definition: The ability to exercise a function across a wide, generated range of inputs.

records.name: Mathematical Assurance
records.definition: The ability to prove mathematically that a system meets its specification.

records.name: Regression Safety
records.definition: The ability to catch regressions when code changes by re-running tests.

records.name: Reliable Automation
records.definition: The ability to automate a process reliably because it repeats identically each run.

records.name: Reliable Testing
records.definition: The ability to test dependably because the same inputs always produce the same outputs.

records.name: Safe Operation
records.definition: The ability to operate without producing incorrect or harmful results.

records.name: Safe Sharing
records.definition: The ability to share data freely across threads because it cannot be modified.

records.name: Specification Compliance
records.definition: The ability to confirm an implementation conforms to its specification.

records.name: Formal Specification
records.definition: A precise, mathematical statement of what a system must do, against which it is proven.

records.name: Ruleset
records.definition: The set of rules a static analyzer checks source code against.

records.name: Tests

distinctFrom.reason: Tests are executable checks, while a specification is the description of required behavior they check against.
Tests are the executable checks, while the test marker names the file that holds one.

records.definition: Executable checks that assert a system behaves as intended.

records.name: Controlled State
records.definition: The requirement that all inputs and state affecting a computation be fixed, bounded or fully specified, so its behavior is reproducible.

records.name: Deterministic Behavior
records.definition: The requirement that the code under test produce the same result for the same inputs.

records.name: No Side Effects
records.definition: The requirement that a function compute its result without observable side effects.

records.name: Properties/Invariants
records.definition: The requirement that the general properties or invariants a function must satisfy be defined.

records.name: Value Semantics
records.definition: The requirement that values be compared and copied by content rather than by reference identity.

records.name: Versioned Inputs
records.definition: The requirement that all inputs to a build or computation be pinned to specific versions.

records.name: Allocation Cost
records.definition: The degree of extra memory allocation incurred by creating new immutable values instead of mutating in place.

records.name: Continuous Updates
records.definition: The degree to which pinning everything for reproducibility conflicts with continuously updating dependencies.

records.name: Cost/Complexity
records.definition: The degree of cost and complexity added by formally proving a system correct.

records.name: Dynamic Runtime Behavior
records.definition: The degree to which runtime-adaptive behavior undermines a system's predictability.

records.name: Encapsulation Extremes
records.definition: The degree to which hiding internals too strictly makes a unit's behavior hard to observe in tests.

records.name: Fitness for Use
records.definition: The degree to which a product meets the needs of its users.

records.name: Real-World Variability
records.definition: The degree to which controlling conditions for repeatability diverges from real-world variability.

records.name: Runtime Adaptivity
records.definition: The degree to which making behavior deterministic limits adapting dynamically at runtime.

records.name: Shrinking/Debug Complexity
records.definition: The degree to which reducing a failing generated case to a minimal example adds debugging complexity.

records.name: Spec Maintenance
records.definition: The degree of ongoing effort to keep a specification current as the system evolves.

records.name: Stateful IO
records.definition: The degree to which stateful input/output conflicts with expressions being replaceable by their values.

records.name: Stateful Operations
records.definition: The degree to which operations that depend on or mutate state conflict with purity.

records.name: Thread Safety
records.definition: The degree to which data can be accessed concurrently without corruption.

records.name: Make Effects Explicit
records.definition: A technique for moving input, output and mutation to named boundary operations, so the code between them stays pure.

records.name: Pass Context Explicitly
records.definition: A technique for passing request, user or tenant context as a parameter or scoped object instead of reading it from global state.

records.name: Inject Clock and Randomness
records.definition: A technique for supplying time and random values through parameters, so the code under test runs the same way every time.

records.name: Test Observable Behavior
records.definition: A technique for asserting on a unit's outputs and effects instead of on the internal calls it makes.

records.name: Fake at the Boundary
records.definition: A technique for replacing an external dependency in tests with a working in-memory implementation of its port.

records.name: Unit Tests
records.definition: A technique for testing one unit of behavior in isolation, fast enough to run on every change.

records.name: Component Tests
records.definition: A technique for testing one deployable component through its public interface with its dependencies replaced.

records.name: Isolate Test State
records.definition: A technique for giving each test its own data and resources, so tests pass in any order.

records.name: Validate at the Boundary
records.definition: A technique for rejecting malformed input where it enters the system, so the core receives only valid values.

records.name: Encapsulate Validation
records.definition: A technique for placing a value's validation in the type that holds it, so every instance is valid.

records.name: Validate as a Group
records.definition: A technique for validating fields that depend on each other together, in the object that groups them.

records.name: Precondition Check
records.definition: A technique for checking at the start of an operation that the state and arguments it requires hold.

records.name: Invariant Check
records.definition: A technique for checking after each change that the rules a state must always satisfy still hold.

records.name: Postcondition Check
records.definition: A technique for checking at the end of an operation that the result and state it promises hold.

records.name: Pin Versions
records.definition: A technique for recording exact versions of dependencies and tools, so every build uses the same inputs.

records.name: Ignored Analyzer Findings
records.definition: A defect in which static analysis findings are left unresolved until the analyzer's output stops being read.
